Interface IuOidcClaims

public interface IuOidcClaims
The standard claims an OpenID Provider may assert about an end user.

One typed accessor per claim OpenID Connect defines, so what a source knows is stated in Java rather than assembled as a document. Nothing here mentions JSON: rendering these claims — into a UserInfo response, into an ID token — belongs to whatever serves them, and a claim's Java type is chosen for what it means rather than for how it prints.

Every claim but sub is optional and defaults to null, so an implementation declares only the attributes its source actually holds and a consumer omits what answers null. That default is what lets a filtered view — one that suppresses the claims a grant's scope doesn't cover — be written as an override of the claims it keeps.

Property names convert to claim names directly under lower case with underscores, so getPreferredUsername() is preferred_username and getEmailVerified() is email_verified. Two claims need a consumer's attention, since a general-purpose converter renders neither the way OpenID Connect requires: updated_at is a NumericDate, seconds since the epoch as a JSON number rather than a formatted timestamp, and address is a nested object rather than a string.

A deployment with claims of its own declares an interface extending this one and renders that type; nothing here is an escape hatch for untyped values.

See Also:

  • Method Details

    • getSub

      String getSub()
      Gets the subject identifier, which names the end user these claims are about.

      The only claim without a default. An OpenID Provider issues it, and a relying party matches what it reads here against the sub of the ID token it holds, refusing the response when the two disagree — so a source's notion of a principal name never overrides the identifier the grant was issued for.

      Returns:
      sub claim

    • getPreferredUsername

      default String getPreferredUsername()
      Gets the shorthand name the end user wishes to be referred to by.

      Unlike sub this is not stable and not guaranteed unique, so a relying party must not key anything by it.

      preferred_username claim; null if not known

    • getEmail

      default String getEmail()
      Gets the end user's preferred email address.

      Not guaranteed unique or stable, and unverified unless separately asserted, so a relying party must not key anything by it.

      Returns:
      email claim; null if not known

    • getEmailVerified

      default Boolean getEmailVerified()
      Reports whether the provider has verified that the end user controls their email address.

      A Boolean rather than a boolean: a provider that has taken no position answers null, which is not the same as answering that the address is unverified.

      Returns:
      email_verified claim; null if the provider asserts nothing
